reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 09 and targeted source-note crop, complete unchanged external-02 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native note crop, full repair-agent white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; rechecked the prior extra-row rejection, right-facing expression, cap emblems, sideburns, moustache, uniform/cross, collar, frame/backplate and transparency.

remaining_reasons: The external-02 repair still has THREE distinct note-mark rows rather than the original TWO: one separate dark horizontal dash near the top, a second row of two gray groups below it, and a third row of two more gray groups. The dark dash is inside the paper and is not its edge. Remove the extra row/dash and restore only the source's two compact upper gray-mark rows in their original footprint and spacing, leaving the lower paper largely blank; do not add or reshuffle replacement marks.
entries.positive_observation: The dark olive cap retains its glossy visor, gold piping/cord, upper eagle emblem and lower wreath/cockade. Covered hair with localized dark sideburns, dark brows and one short upper-lip moustache remain without a chin/jaw beard or glasses. The head and gaze face image right, and the single slightly parted mouth retains a small pale tooth edge. The dark high-collared uniform retains one pale-edged dark cross, and the rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The complete dark frame, opaque muted warm grey-olive backplate, cream note and right-edge contour remain; the lower paper is largely blank. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring. These properties do not resolve the persistent third note row.
entries.visible_limitations: Fine cap embroidery, moustache/mouth pixels and collar-cross detail are too small to transcribe at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The source-page crop clearly shows two compact upper rows, while the native repair crop distinctly resolves three; the rejection is based on visible row count, not unreadable lettering or alpha values.
